absent: Complete SNP launch update flow beyond the visible prologue that stops at slot lookup.
Full receive start and query length logic preceding the visible tail.
Firmware numeric command identifiers and error code meanings.
Lifetime and locking rules for SEV info handles ASIDs and region lists outside shown paths.
Internals of cache writeback RMP transition and guest memory backend helpers.
User ABI numeric values and structure layouts for SEV SNP command payloads.
Scheduling and vCPU locking guarantees assumed by migration transfer.

findings.text: Receive update handling applies only to SEV guests, obtains a user supplied control structure, rejects missing header guest or transport locations or sizes, keeps the guest extent inside a single page, duplicates the two firmware blobs into kernel memory, pins one guest page writable, performs cache maintenance, issues the firmware receive update operation against the pinned address with the memory encryption mask asserted, then unpins and frees resources.
Guest extent is accepted only when length is positive and bounded by the page size and when the page offset plus length does not cross into the next page.
Receive finish handling accepts only SEV guests and relays the stored firmware handle to the firmware receive finish operation with caller visible error reporting.

Mirroring VMs are restricted to command KVM_SEV_LAUNCH_UPDATE_VMSA plus command KVM_SEV_GUEST_STATUS plus commands KVM_SEV_DBG_DECRYPT and KVM_SEV_DBG_ENCRYPT; every other operation identifier is refused.

Acquiring two VMs for migration first rejects identical source and destination, claims per VM migration progress markers with acquiring exchange to serialize concurrent attempts, then takes the destination VM mutex in killable form followed by the source VM mutex with a nesting level, unwinding markers and any held mutex on interruption or failure, while the paired release drops both mutexes and clears both markers with release ordering.

Migration transfer preserves source cache behavior by writing back before deactivating source, then moves active state plus address space identifier firmware handle locked page accounting and ES related flags to the destination while clearing the source, transfers region tracking and mirror membership lists, reassigns owner back pointers and VM references under a dedicated mirror mutex, reinitializes each destination control area, and for ES capable VMs copies per vCPU protected state and control addresses while resetting the source entries to invalid and clearing protection.
Source cache maintenance must happen before clearing source active status so later reclaim still observes an SEV VM.
Mirror list surgery during transfer is serialized by a global mirror mutex, while the transfer itself runs with both VM mutexes and all vCPU locks already held by the move entry.

Move of encryption context from another VM file descriptor validates the descriptor and its VM operations, locks the pair, rejects mismatched VM types or an already protected destination or a non protected or SNP source, reconciles misc cgroup charging when owners differ, locks all vCPUs on both sides, validates source vCPUs, allocates fresh CPU tracking for the destination, performs the state move, marks the source dead, and finally unwinds charges cgroup references vCPU locks and pair locks.
For ES capable sources the destination must have the same online vCPU count and every source vCPU must already be in protected state; non ES sources impose no extra checks.
Helper reports whether a file object represents a KVM VM by comparing its operation vector against the VM operations table and handling null input as false.
Public move entry transfers an SEV context from a source VM designated by file descriptor into the calling VM and returns standard negative errno values on validation locking or resource failures.
Device attribute query serves the x86 SEV group and exposes supported VMSA features plus supported SNP policy bits plus an SNP certificate request flag, rejecting other groups or attributes.

Device query ABI centers on group KVM_X86_GRP_SEV with attributes KVM_X86_SEV_VMSA_FEATURES and KVM_X86_SNP_POLICY_BITS and KVM_X86_SEV_SNP_REQ_CERTS selecting respectively feature mask and policy mask and certificate need flag.

Per vCPU initialization enables SEV controls, relaxes traps that require guest memory inspection, and dispatches to SNP protected state handling on creation events and to ES specific initialization when appropriate.
SEV control initialization always sets the SEV enable bit and disables undefined and general protection fault interceptions that cannot be serviced without decrypting guest memory.

SNP secondary creation event handling runs under the per vCPU VMSA mutex, ignores spurious events when no thread waits for reset, otherwise clears the wait marker, parks the vCPU halted and not unhalted, consumes and invalidates the pending VMSA address, reloads the VMSA, and marks the vCPU runnable when the consumed address was valid even on reload failure so that entry fails promptly rather than blocking forever.

VMSA reload asserts ownership of the per vCPU SNP VMSA mutex, publishes invalidation of control and tracked guest addresses with single ordered stores, refreshes the full control area, resolves the backing private page through the memory slot and guest memory backend, then under read mode memory management lock records the guest address and either requests a deferred reload when the slot changed concurrently or installs the hardware address, finally releasing the backend page reference.

ES control initialization enables ES controls, installs the VMSA address without encryption mask when a host allocated area exists and an invalid marker otherwise or when a guest supplied VMSA already took over, advertises allowed feature bits when the platform supports them, removes hypervisor traps on control registers and extended control writes that the hypervisor cannot emulate, tracks control and extended feature changes through dedicated traps, adjusts debug register and debug fault trapping based on debug swap capability, and refreshes the guest communication block address on non creation paths.
Guest communication block reporting stores the supplied value into the control area guest communication field.
SNP guest predicate is build dependent, consulting VM state when SNP support is compiled in and constantly reporting false otherwise.

SNP context bring up allocates an accounted firmware page, translates it for the security processor, requests context creation, and on success later binds the VM address space identifier to that context through an activate command; allocation or firmware failure releases the page and yields no context.

SNP launch start rejects non SNP VMs, user copy failures, repeated context allocation, nonzero flags, policy bits outside the supported mask, missing mandatory policy bits, and missing default TSC rate when secure TSC is enabled, and on firmware or bind failure tears down the freshly created context to avoid leaking firmware state.

SNP context teardown is a no operation when no context exists, otherwise translates the context address, serializes the firmware decommission that unbinds the address space identifier under a global deactivate write lock, warns on firmware failure, and frees the firmware page while clearing the pointer.
Populate argument bundle carries a page type byte plus the security processor file descriptor used for firmware calls plus a field for firmware reported error codes.

Post populate handling for SNP launch update first verifies the target frame has an initial shared platform state and fails on lookup error or prior assignment, optionally copies a source page into the destination, transitions the frame to private bound to the guest address and VM identifier, submits the firmware launch update for a small page of the requested type, and on firmware failure reclaims the frame while copying back firmware supplied diagnostic content into a dirty source page for CPUID type validation failures.
Launch update prefix resolves SEV VM state and initializes an empty populate argument bundle plus user parameters and slot lookup before the truncated remainder.
An architecturally invalid page marker represents absence of VMSA or communication control addresses and of pending guest VMSA state.
SNP launch lifecycle progresses from absent context to allocated context to firmware started to ASID bound, with any failure after allocation returning to absent through decommission.
